# Security Checklist: XPLAT-005 Read-Only Helper Port

**Purpose**: Validate that the XPLAT-005 spec and plan define enough security requirements for shell-free helper ports, safe path handling, Python-standard-library-only execution, and read-only boundaries before tasks are generated.
**Created**: 2026-07-02
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This checklist is generated by the `$speckit-checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.

## Shell And Subprocess Safety

- [x] CHK001 Do the spec and plan require promoted helper behavior to run without Bash, `jq`, shell parsing, process substitution, or Unix-only command assumptions? [Spec FR-009/FR-010; Plan Technical Context]
- [x] CHK002 Do the spec or plan explicitly prohibit `shell=True`, shell-command strings, `os.system`, and shell interpolation in new Python helper ports and Bash-reference comparison harnesses, while requiring argv-list subprocess calls when subprocesses are unavoidable? [Resolved: Spec §FR-026, Plan §Error And Security Requirements, Data Model §Bash Reference Comparison, and promotion-record schema `subprocess_policy` now require argv-only subprocess handling.]
- [x] CHK003 Are subprocess safety cases named as permitted golden-only fixtures so helper ports can prove no-shell behavior without relying on live Bash behavior? [Spec Parity And Promotion Rules; Plan Helper Promotion Matrix Plan]
- [x] CHK004 Are rejected subprocess or prerequisite failures required to preserve deterministic diagnostics and exit semantics rather than leaking host-specific shell errors? [Spec FR-007/FR-008; Data Model Helper Invocation Result]

## Path Handling And Trust Boundaries

- [x] CHK005 Are Windows-style paths, paths with spaces, source-checkout relative paths, and no-Bash behavior included in required fixture coverage? [Spec Acceptance Scenarios; Spec Assumptions; Plan Target Platform]
- [x] CHK006 Are helper request paths required to use typed-path primitives instead of shell parsing or ad hoc string command construction? [Data Model Helper Invocation Request; Plan Technical Context]
- [x] CHK007 Do the spec or plan require filesystem inputs to resolve symlinks and relative components against the repo/plugin trust boundary, rejecting traversal or symlink escapes before reading helper inputs? [Resolved: Spec §FR-027, Plan §Error And Security Requirements, Data Model §Trusted Path Input, request schema path inputs, and promotion-record schema `path_boundary_policy` now require boundary checks.]
- [x] CHK008 Are path normalization rules limited to explicitly volatile fields so parity cannot hide changed counts, booleans, statuses, diagnostic codes, public text, stderr, or exit codes? [Spec Parity And Promotion Rules; Data Model Normalization Rule]
- [x] CHK009 Does the plan avoid native Windows support claims while still requiring deterministic synthetic Windows/path fixtures before helper promotion? [Spec Assumptions; Plan Target Platform; Workflow Success Criteria Summary]

## Dependency And Supply-Chain Surface

- [x] CHK010 Do requirements lock new helper logic to Python 3.11+ standard library only? [Spec FR-009; Plan Language/Version]
- [x] CHK011 Do requirements exclude new package installs, virtualenv restore, network access, Node, PowerShell, Go, Rust, Zig, and `jq` for promoted helper execution? [Spec FR-010; Plan Performance Goals]
- [x] CHK012 Does the declared file plan avoid package-manager manifests, dependency lockfiles, installer behavior, generated payloads, marketplace metadata, and public documentation surfaces, while limiting runner source manifest/checksum updates to existing XPLAT-004 metadata? [Plan Declared File Operations; Spec FR-021; Spec FR-028]
- [x] CHK013 Are XPLAT-004 runner manifest/checksum controls reused as existing runner metadata rather than expanding XPLAT-005 into a new supply-chain mechanism? [XPLAT-004 Archive Report; Plan Primary Dependencies]

## Read-Only And Mutation Boundaries

- [x] CHK014 Do requirements explicitly exclude mutation helpers that write PR packets, generate PR bodies, emit split PR state, restack, relocate artifacts, install agents, modify generated payloads, or mutate repo/user-local state? [Spec FR-005; Spec Scope Boundaries]
- [x] CHK015 Are mixed-mode helpers split so only read-only `generate-spec-index --check`, `plan-layers <feature-dir>`, and `validate-pr-packet` validation output/diagnostics/exit behavior are in scope? [Spec Helper And Mode Matrix; Plan Slice 2]
- [x] CHK016 Does the helper registry model require `mode=read_only`, `writes_state=false`, and pre-execution rejection of unknown helper ids or mutation modes? [Data Model Helper Registry Entry; Data Model Helper Invocation Request; Contract Schema]
- [x] CHK017 Does the promotion matrix label mutation-adjacent helpers and modes as `out_of_scope` with XPLAT-006 or later follow-up instead of leaving ambiguous statuses? [Plan Helper Promotion Matrix Plan; Spec Promotion Record]
- [x] CHK018 Does the verification plan include a scope audit for zero active Claude/Codex skill, hook, generated payload, install, marketplace/public-doc, mutation-helper, PR-emission, split-state, restack, relocation, install repair, or autoheal cutover edits? [Plan Verification Plan; Spec SC-005]

## Release-Gate Evidence

- [x] CHK019 Are Python tests promoted to authoritative security-relevant gates only after golden fixture parity and Bash-reference comparison are accepted per helper? [Spec FR-011 through FR-015; Plan Helper Promotion Matrix Plan]
- [x] CHK020 Does the PR review packet requirement force known gaps to distinguish unpromoted Bash-reference helpers from out-of-scope mutation or active-cutover helpers? [Spec PR Review Packet Requirements]
- [x] CHK021 Is local smoke evidence scoped to source-checkout `runtime-info` only, with installed-cache launch, helper parity, mutation safety, and full native matrix support explicitly unsupported? [Spec Local Source-Checkout Smoke Boundary; Data Model Source-Checkout Smoke Evidence]
- [x] CHK022 Are project constitution safety principles reflected in the plan, especially no new Bash scripts, no unchecked shell behavior, test coverage before merge, and simple explicit registry design? [Constitution Script Safety; Plan Constitution Check]
